chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'The eater of usury (interest), the one who feeds it, its scribe, and its witness are equal.'
ai.seo_question: Who are the four parties considered equal in the ruling of usury according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the legal equality of the four main parties in a usury transaction: the consumer, the provider, the recorder, and the witness, signifying they share equally in the ruling and liability. In Shia jurisprudence, this underscores the comprehensive nature of riba, extending its prohibition beyond the primary borrowers and lenders to include those who document and attest to the contract, thereby ensuring the integrity of the entire transaction. This principle highlights the communal responsibility in avoiding interest, reinforcing the severity of riba as a major sin in Islamic law.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, form his father, from Ibn Abu Najran, from Aasim Bin Humeyd, from Muhammad Bin Qays, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The eater of the interest and its feeder, and its contractor, and its witness with regards to it are equal’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu Najran from ‘Asim ibn Hamid from m h ibn Qays, who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that Amir al-Mu’minin, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
One who consumes Riba’, one who feeds Riba ’ and one who documents it, are all the same (in committing this sins).”’
